title: Cost every plate, protect allergic guests, get paid safely

say: Cost every plate, protect allergic guests, and get paid safely.
This is the video for module three of Catering Basics and Food Safety: costing, allergens and running a professional service.
Many home cooks price by feel, then finish a big job tired, with almost nothing left. The cure is a costing sheet.

panel.heading: Good food at a loss is not a business
items: Count every naira, including hidden costs

say: Every naira you will spend, divided by the number of plates, plus the profit you choose.

say: Let us follow Ronke. These prices are approximate examples only. Use your own market prices on the day you quote.
Ingredients come to about 224,200 naira. Chicken alone is 126,000 of that, over 40 percent of the total.
Then the hidden costs people forget. Gas, about 12,000. Packs, spoons and nylon for 110 packs, about 22,000.
Transport, about 15,000. And two helpers at 10,000 each, 20,000.
The total job cost is 293,200 naira. Divided by 100 plates, each plate costs about 2,932 naira. Anything below that loses money.

Markup is profit as a percentage of cost. Margin is profit as a percentage of the selling price. Mixing them up is why many caterers earn less than they think. To price with margin, divide the cost by 1 minus the margin.

panel.heading: Margin, not markup
items: Date your prices; quote valid 7 days

say: Ronke wants a 30% margin, so she divides 2,932 by 0.70. That gives 4,189 naira.

panel.heading: Margin, not markup
items: Date your prices; quote valid 7 days

say: She rounds to 4,200 per plate. For 100 plates, that is 420,000 naira, with about 126,800 profit.

panel.heading: Margin, not markup
items: Date your prices; quote valid 7 days

say: Market prices can rise before the event, so write that the quote is valid for 7 days. And pay yourself through a labour line, separate from profit. Never cut cost by cutting food safety.

panel.heading: Margin, not markup
items: Date your prices; quote valid 7 days
panel.rule: A 30% markup is not a 30% margin.

say: A food allergy can be severe and life-threatening, and cooking does not remove most allergens. Even a trace from a shared spoon can be enough. Groundnut hides in suya spice, kuli-kuli and some small chops.

items: Groundnut: suya spice, kuli-kuli, small chops

Wheat: meat pie, chin chin, wrappers

say: Ask every client about allergies, and write the answer on the job sheet, not only in a chat. Halima's client said the bride's sister has a severe groundnut allergy.

say: She handed it to the client personally. If a guest asks and you are not sure, say: I am not sure, so please do not eat it. If someone has trouble breathing or swelling after eating, call for emergency help and get them to a hospital immediately.

panel.rule: Not sure? Say: please do not eat it. Never guess.

say: Ronke's quote of 420,000 naira asks for a 50% deposit, 210,000, before she buys any ingredient. The balance is due two days before the event. She confirms every payment in her banking app and sends a receipt with the amount, date and balance remaining.

panel.heading: Get paid the safe way
right: Fund a party from your pocket

say: Fraudsters send fake SMS and screenshot alerts. Never trust them. Write your guest-count and cancellation terms on the quote, so they are agreed before any money moves.

panel.heading: Get paid the safe way
right: Fund a party from your pocket

say: To remember. Count every cost and divide by the plates. Price with margin, not markup. Cook allergen-free meals first, sealed and labelled. Take a deposit before you shop. And confirm payments in your banking app, never by SMS alone.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Count every cost, then divide by plates
Confirm payments in your banking app

say: Now practise. Cost one menu package with current market prices. Write ingredient cards and mark the allergens. And create your quotation, event record and feedback message templates.
